question.text: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and the Maintenance of Records Rules, an AIF (as a reporting entity) must maintain records of which of the following cash transactions?

answer.text: Only cash transactions exceeding INR 50 lakh; cross-border transfers are reported by authorized dealers only
Only transactions by non-resident investors exceeding INR 1 crore
All transactions, regardless of amount, via Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) only
All cash transactions of more than INR 10 lakh, all integrally-connected series within a month exceeding INR 10 lakh in aggregate, and all cross-border wire transfers exceeding INR 5 lakh

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 12 PMLA read with Maintenance of Records Rules, reporting entities (including AIFs) must maintain records of: (i) cash transactions > INR 10 lakh; (ii) series of integrally-connected cash transactions in a month aggregating > INR 10 lakh; (iii) NPO receipts > INR 10 lakh; (iv) cross-border wire transfers > INR 5 lakh; (v) forged/counterfeit-currency transactions; (vi) all suspicious transactions regardless of value/cash-or-non-cash. **The Trap:** Option B uses an incorrect threshold. Option C scopes only to non-residents. Option D misses the CTR thresholds — STRs are in addition to CTRs, not a replacement. **Cross-Exam Context:** Core XXIV (AML Officer) question. XIX-C tests it from AIF-Principal-Officer angle. III-A/C also tests PMLA thresholds. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: Appoint a Principal Officer (PO) to liaise with FIU-India; file CTRs on cash threshold; STR on any suspicious activity irrespective of amount. Register with CKYCR within 10 days of client relationship; for FPIs, use KRA portal with risk-based KYC. Maintain records for 5 years post-transaction-cessation.
